messages:
Luis (CS): Heads-up — customer reported duplicate partial generations + double billing after a short SSE disconnect. Ticket INC-8372. Repro steps attached.
Eve (CS): Ugh. Do we know if they hit resume token mismatch or if client retried without idempotency key? :grimacing:
Luis (CS): They were on a mobile client with flaky LTE. App logs show immediate reconnect within 200ms and client sends a new connect with the same session_id but no idempotency-key header.
Raj (Infra): Can you paste the raw connect payload/headers from the client and the server side accept log lines?
Luis (CS): Client connect snippet:
```
GET /v1/stream?model=redwood-xl HTTP/1.1
Authorization: Bearer xxxxx
X-Session-Id: sess-9021
X-Resume-Token: resume_0001
Accept: text/event-stream
```
Server accepted and returned 200 then streamed two partial chunks, then disconnect.
Eve (CS): And billing shows two generation units charged? One for original, one after recon.
Luis (CS): Yes. Customer repro steps:
1) Start streaming gen (mobile). 2) Kill data for ~100-300ms. 3) Client auto-reconnect immediately and re-sends connect with same X-Resume-Token but *no* Idempotency header. 4) Server resumed but also started a fresh generation race and sent an overlapping chunk.
Olga (Eng): That sounds like a race between resume flow and fallback spawn of a new generator. We saw an edge case where heartbeat flip (fast reconnect) causes state machine to treat connection as new before resume handshake completes.
Anya (SRE): Do we have timestamps from the runtime logs around connection id sess-9021? I want the sequence: accept -> disconnect -> reconnect -> resume vs spawn.
Luis (CS): Pasted runtime excerpt from their region (eu-west-1):
```
[2026-03-14T12:01:10.123Z] conn sess-9021 accept resume_token=resume_0001
[2026-03-14T12:01:10.420Z] conn sess-9021 stream chunk id=abc123
[2026-03-14T12:01:10.430Z] conn sess-9021 disconnect client-closed
[2026-03-14T12:01:10.635Z] conn sess-9021 reconnect attempt resume_token=resume_0001
[2026-03-14T12:01:10.636Z] conn sess-9021 resume-success state=attached
[2026-03-14T12:01:10.637Z] conn sess-9021 spawn-fallback new-gen-id=def456
[2026-03-14T12:01:10.638Z] conn sess-9021 stream chunk id=def456-a
```
Olga (Eng): There — at 636 we resume, but at 637 we also spawned fallback. Spawn is supposed to be gated while resume handshake completes. Looks like timing window small with <2ms gap.
Raj (Infra): That gating logic was hardened last quarter but there was a micro-optimization that trades strict gating for lower latency. Looks like a regression in the fast-path.
Anya (SRE): Impact: duplicate generations and double billing. Likely customers with aggressive client reconnect/backoff <250ms are affected.
Eve (CS): Customer asked for mitigation ASAP. Can we suggest a client-side workaround until fix is deployed?
Olga (Eng): Workarounds:
- Client must send idempotency-key header on reconnect (X-Idempotency-Key) so server dedupes duplicate generation spawn.
- Or add a small jittered backoff (>=350ms) before auto-reconnect.
Luis (CS): I'll pass both options to the customer. They prefer not to change app quickly. Any quick server-side knobs we can toggle for that customer only?
Raj (Infra): We can enable stricter resume gating for a specific tenant by flipping "resume_strict_mode" on their tenant config (region-level feature flag). That prevents spawn until resume confirmed.
Olga (Eng): I'll open a hotfix PR to reintroduce the gating check on the fast path and add a defensive check for duplicate spawn within 10ms of resume. Target patch on canary within 2 hrs.
Eve (CS): Please also add a billing safe-guard — if two generators are started within X ms for same session/resume token, mark the second as a dedupe and don't bill pending verification.
Raj (Infra): We have a temporary billing-exclusion label we can apply to the runtime for that tenant. I'll coordinate with finance after patch.
Luis (CS): Thanks. Customer escalation note: added mitigation, asked for ETA. They're happy with toggle if rollout is quick. Ticket updated: https://redwood.internal/INC-8372 :eyes:
deploy-bot: deploy queued: hotfix/resume-gating -> canary eu-west-1 (PR #5012)
Olga (Eng): Will monitor canary logs and post results here. If green, roll to prod and follow up with billing exclusion and postmortem.
Eve (CS): Thanks team — please @Luis when you have ETA for customer. :thumbsup:
